svg.title: From Fragmented Listings to a Firm Max Bid
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-finding-and-bidding-the-sale; chapter number: 1; title: From Fragmented Listings to a Firm Max Bid; subtitle: The five-step loop practitioners run before any government surplus bid; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Map the platforms; value: Step 1; detail: Delaware, New Castle County, and Wilmington each sold through a different platform; GSA Auctions, GovDeals, Public Surplus, and Municibid are the core channels, with no dealer license required.; step: 02; label: Pull historical sold prices; value: Step 2; detail: Search US Gov Bid past auctions going back years to see what everything sold for before setting a max.; step: 03; label: Read the terms of sale; value: Step 3; detail: Payment method and deadline, a GovDeals buyer's premium of 5% to 12.5%, the pickup window, and title versus bill of sale.; step: 04; label: Inspect or send an inspector; value: Step 4; detail: Walk from poke-through frame rust, flood signs, or a mismatched VIN; if inspection day is impossible, hire a mobile ASE-certified inspection service where the yard allows it.; step: 05; label: Set a firm max bid and hold it; value: Step 5; detail: Price in sales tax, buyer's premiums, and shipping, then write the number down; if bidding passes it, let it go.; caption: Keyed vehicles at Norfolk government auctions had a $1,300 middle price versus $550 without keys, and Public Surplus caps card purchases at $4,000, so the terms decide the real price.; assumptions note: All figures are attributed practitioner claims; premiums are set by each selling municipality and vary by listing.; note: Attributed to East Coast Classics (q09PUtJPIxs), UX Auctions (Z87d62pWVEk), GovAuctions (Ie7zxVOXjeE), and The Salmon Runs (jaeWKn_Nu68).

circle.title: step: 01; label: Map the platforms; value: Step 1; detail: Delaware, New Castle County, and Wilmington each sold through a different platform; GSA Auctions, GovDeals, Public Surplus, and Municibid are the core channels, with no dealer license required.

text.title: Delaware, New Castle County, and Wilmington each sold through a different platform; GSA Auctions, GovDeals, Public Surplus, and Municibid are the core channels, with no dealer license required.

circle.title: step: 02; label: Pull historical sold prices; value: Step 2; detail: Search US Gov Bid past auctions going back years to see what everything sold for before setting a max.

text.title: Search US Gov Bid past auctions going back years to see what everything sold for before setting a max.

circle.title: step: 03; label: Read the terms of sale; value: Step 3; detail: Payment method and deadline, a GovDeals buyer's premium of 5% to 12.5%, the pickup window, and title versus bill of sale.

text.title: Payment method and deadline, a GovDeals buyer's premium of 5% to 12.5%, the pickup window, and title versus bill of sale.

circle.title: step: 04; label: Inspect or send an inspector; value: Step 4; detail: Walk from poke-through frame rust, flood signs, or a mismatched VIN; if inspection day is impossible, hire a mobile ASE-certified inspection service where the yard allows it.

text.title: Walk from poke-through frame rust, flood signs, or a mismatched VIN; if inspection day is impossible, hire a mobile ASE-certified inspection service where the yard allows it.

circle.title: step: 05; label: Set a firm max bid and hold it; value: Step 5; detail: Price in sales tax, buyer's premiums, and shipping, then write the number down; if bidding passes it, let it go.
